A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CDKA research work and contain 23 readable pages, including Appendices A–F. Full text and rendered-page comparison support reliable assessment of the text, equations, figures, and tables.

before.justification: v2 reports original CDKA fine-tuning experiments on language and image tasks, component-design and stabilization ablations, and computational measurements in Sections 3–4 and Appendix F.

after.justification: v3 retains these original CDKA experiments, ablations, and computational measurements. Its use of previously published baseline results does not change the presence of the authors' own empirical results.

M1.justification: The Kronecker-sum formulation, component-design guidelines, initialization, stabilization factor, and efficient computation remain identical in Sections 2–4.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same five GLUE tasks, MetaMathQA/GSM8k, Code-FeedBack/HumanEval, and seven image-classification datasets. The appendix evaluation scenarios are also retained.

E2.justification: Table 13 removes LoRA+ and adds GoRA to the CLIP-ViT-B/16 comparison, using results attributed to He et al. (2025). GoRA already appears in the language-task comparisons, but its participation in this image-classification comparison is new. Other comparator sets are unchanged.

E3.justification: Sections 3–4 and Appendix A retain the same training subsets, metrics, model configurations, hyperparameters, and testing procedures. The revised tables do not report changed experimental settings.

E4.justification: Appendix F revises the aggregate evidence for the existing r1 and r2 sensitivity studies through corrected CLIP averages in Tables 18–19. Table 19 now shows monotonically increasing average performance with r2. The sweep configurations and individual dataset scores are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions state that results are reported as means and standard deviations over three random seeds. Individual standard-deviation values change in Table 13, but reporting practices, run counts, and statistical procedures do not.

E6.justification: Table 13 replaces LoRA+ results (83.57 average) with GoRA results (89.47), changes RESISC45 scores for DoRA from 90.32 to 90.03 and LoRA-GA from 94.33 to 94.43, and revises three standard deviations. CDKA retains its 90.08 average; GoRA becomes best on SUN397 with 76.46 versus CDKA's 76.42. Table 18 corrects CLIP averages from 89.69 to 87.26 and 88.70 to 84.14; Table 19 corrects 89.69 to 87.26. The unchanged per-dataset scores establish these appendix changes as summary corrections.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, Theorems 3.2 and 3.4, and derivations and proofs in Appendices B–E are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about component design, subspace alignment, stabilization, parameter efficiency, and cross-task performance.

C2.justification: The explanations of component design and training stability, robustness interpretations, and limitation to linear theoretical settings remain unchanged. The corrected appendix averages support an existing interpretation rather than introduce a new one.

D1.justification: Implementation details, tuned layers, Appendix A hyperparameters, hardware information, and the stated code location are unchanged. The abstract's code link is merely rewrapped.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, research positioning, and reference list are identical. GoRA and He et al. (2025) were already cited, so the additional Table 13 comparison introduces no new cited work.

P1.justification: The abstract changes a dash in 'parameter-budget-aware', and the arXiv version/date stamp is updated. Otherwise, prose, terminology, section order, and appendix organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 13 changes comparator rows and updates bold/underlined ranking highlights. The abstract's line wrapping also changes. Figures, other table structures, and their placement remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The corrected averages in Tables 18–19 now agree with the listed scores and remove the apparent contradiction between Table 19's aggregate trend and its interpretation. Table 13 adds a competitive GoRA comparison while dropping LoRA+. These provide a limited improvement in numerical reliability and comparison evidence; the core work is unchanged, and a pre-existing DoRA averaging inconsistency remains in Table 13 (83.48 reported versus approximately 83.60 from v3's listed scores).
